date_note: Security.nl's article of 25 November is the only page read and gives no earlier day for the report's publication.
exec: DIVD's report says an attacker used two Zammad zero-days and ARP spoofing to take data; two Zammad instances were unpatched.
geo_basis: country (the Netherlands), as DIVD is described as a Dutch institute
plain: DIVD, a Dutch security group, published a forensic report on its own hack. It says the attacker used two Zammad flaws, then ARP spoofing to move inside the network and take data.
summary: Security.nl reports that DIVD published a forensic report by Merlon on its breach. According to the report, the attacker used two Zammad zero-days, stole thousands of email addresses and research past its disclosure limit, then used ARP spoofing to intercept traffic to the PostgreSQL servers behind Jira and Confluence. The report says two Zammad instances had not been patched for a year.
title: DIVD report: attacker used two Zammad zero-days, then ARP spoofing, to take data

validation.note: Only Security.nl (relaying DIVD's published report) was read; DIVD's own report and Merlon's findings were not opened.

action: DIVD's report recommends patching promptly, keeping sensitive services off the internet, encrypting internal traffic and strictly segmenting networks.
